title: Ritual: Tribute, Favours, Omens and the Rite of the Nameless
summary: How Ritual works in Path of Exile 2 from altar activation and Tribute through Favours, Omens, Audience with the King, the Rite of the Nameless chain and the Bodach gate.
description: A reference for the Ritual end-game system in Path of Exile 2: activating altars, earning Tribute, the Favours decision, Omen priority, King progress, the Rite of the Nameless map chain and the Bodach access boundary.
prerequisites: Maps unlocked and you can sustain Waystones
A character that survives being surrounded at the altar
At least one Audience with the King banked
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: King in the Mists, the Ritual pinnacle boss of Path of Exile 2

items.title: What activates a Ritual?
body: Ritual altars appear in maps. Activating one pulls nearby monsters into the circle and revives them across waves until you clear the circle.
Each cleared altar banks Tribute. Later altars in the same map can hold more, so the last ritual is usually the richest.

items.title: What are Favours for?
body: Favours are the menu that opens at a ritual. You spend Tribute to Purchase items, Defer them to the next ritual, Reroll the options, or Offer Tribute toward the King.

items.title: How do I reach the King in the Mists?
body: Audience with the King is the key item. Bank one and use it to open the King in the Mists, the Ritual pinnacle boss.

items.title: What comes after the King?
body: After the King you begin the Rite of the Nameless chain: collect body parts, assemble the Effigy and claim the Foretold Bounty, which gates the Bodach step.

sections.title: How a Ritual map flows
paragraphs: Ritual maps contain one or more altars. Clear the map normally, then activate each altar to spawn its wave; the map does not pause while you fight, so clear threats first.
Tribute stacks across altars in the same map. The final altar is where big purchases happen, so keep Tribute for it rather than spending early.
Deferring an item pushes it to the next altar in the same map; it does not vanish, but you must reach that altar to claim it.
bullets: Altars spawn waves, map keeps running

sections.title: Tribute budget planner
paragraphs: Plan your Tribute before the last altar. Decide whether you are hunting a specific unique, farming Omens, or just banking currency.
Defer expensive items you cannot afford yet; they carry to the next altar and may become affordable as Tribute grows across the map.
Reroll only when the board has nothing worth your Tribute. A reroll costs Tribute and can still return poor options, so use it sparingly.

sections.title: The Rite of the Nameless route
paragraphs: After the King falls, the Rite of the Nameless begins. It is a map chain where you collect body parts dropped by Rite encounters.
Assemble the parts into the Effigy at the ritual site. The Effigy is what drives the Foretold Bounty step of the chain.
This chain assumes a character that already beat the King; do not start it under-geared, as the encounters scale up through the chain.

sections.title: Reaching the Bodach gate
paragraphs: The Bodach step is the end of the Rite chain opened by the Foretold Bounty. It is the deepest Ritual content and assumes a fully geared character.
Treat Bodach as a pinnacle gate: arrive with your defensive board intact and your damage confirmed, because the encounter scales past the King.
This guide covers the path and preparation; the boss page covers Bodach's attacks in detail once it is reachable.

sections.title: Solo vs party
sections.intro: How Ritual behaves alone versus in a group.

tabs.label: Solo
paragraphs: Solo you keep all Tribute and all Favours decisions are yours. Defer and reroll freely because only you consume the board.
The downside is surviving every altar wave alone, so defensive setup matters more than in a group.

tabs.label: Party
paragraphs: In a party, altar waves are shared and easier to clear, but Tribute and Favours are split by the host rules of the instance.
Confirm who is the host and how rewards are assigned before the map, since progress and loot can differ from solo runs.
bullets: Tribute and Favours split by host
Agree on host and loot first

sections.title: What players report
sections.intro: Community experiences; treat as strategy, not guaranteed math.

cards.title: Save Tribute for the last altar
body: Players consistently report the final altar holds the best items, so spending early wastes Tribute.

cards.title: Defer beats reroll
body: Most lost wanted items were rerolled away; deferring to the next altar keeps them alive.

cards.title: King progress stalls on host rules
body: Party King progress often differs from solo because of how the instance assigns the gate.

sections.title: Common problems
paragraphs: If your King progress never advances, check you actually used the Audience and killed the King; the Rite chain only starts after the kill.
If a wanted item vanished, you likely rerolled it instead of deferring; reroll only on a dead board.
If party loot feels wrong, confirm host and assignment rules before the map, since they differ from solo.
bullets: No King progress = no Audience used or not killed
